name: Saddam Hussein
role: President of Iraq (1979-2003) and leader of the Ba'ath Party
summary: Saddam Hussein ruled Iraq as a single-party Ba'athist state combining Arab nationalism, state-planned socialism with a limited private sector, and personal authoritarian rule. He nationalised oil, promoted women's education and work, fought wars with Iran and Kuwait, and suppressed Kurdish, Shia and party opponents; from 1991-93 his regime moved from secular Ba'athism to a state religious campaign.

public-ownership.rationale: Nationalised the Iraqi oil industry in 1972 and cited it as the core of the revolution; the constitution he presided under states that national resources and basic means of production are owned by the people.

national-resource-control.rationale: Led the 1972-73 nationalisation of the foreign oil companies and described it as the revolution's defining act against imperialism.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Told the press in 1980 that private property continues only 'provided it is socially acceptable', i.e. without a material base giving a minority political or social influence at the people's expense; the constitution calls ownership a social function.

property-fundamental.rationale: Said private property is to be tolerated only within limits set by the socialist programme; the constitution allows expropriation for public interest and bars it where it conflicts with state planning.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Ran five-year development plans (e.g. 1981-85) and Iraq's constitution makes the state responsible for planning, directing and steering the national economy; he said the state holds 'the central links'.

central-planning.rationale: Governed through national development plans with the state holding the central economic links while allowing a private sector; his stated model was planned socialism with private activity alongside.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Said the socialist sector holds the central links and sets a prices policy that cannot be violated without punishment, letting only 'remoter elements' move freely; private activity is encouraged but guided by the state.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rejected the Marxist view that surplus value means exploitation: 'We may have surplus value without exploitation'; an Iraqi working for the private sector 'is not exploited'.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The constitution under his rule commits the state to free medical services in protection, treatment and medicine in cities and rural areas; he said every Iraqi has a guaranteed source of living.

free-public-college.rationale: The constitution under his rule guarantees free education at primary, secondary and university stages.

job-guarantee.rationale: Said every Iraqi who can work 'has an open chance with the State at all times'; the constitution declares work a right ensured to every able citizen.

cut-welfare.rationale: Described a system in which every Iraqi has a permanent source of living, including those who cannot work who receive a wage equal to an unskilled labourer's, and expanded social security in the constitution.

land-redistribution.rationale: His government's Agrarian Reform Law (which he cited) capped agricultural holdings; the constitution gives the surplus above the legal maximum to the people.

collective-farming.rationale: Supported enlarging individual farmers' allotments of land in 1980 as long as this did not create social or political influence contrary to socialism, rather than collectivising farms.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The constitution of his government prohibits immobile (real estate) ownership by non-Iraqis except where a law allows.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Said Ba'ath socialism differs basically from other socialist systems (keeps private property alongside a socialist sector) and the constitution lists struggle against capitalistic ideology among education goals; also distanced Ba'athism from Marxist class doctrine.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Said private activity should extend in services, production, agriculture and industry within limits, and defended larger farmer allotments, but also kept key sectors in state hands.

class-collaboration.rationale: Inferred: his government rejected orthodox Marxist class conflict, built a National Front with other parties, and said workers in the private sector are not exploited when the state guarantees work.

one-party-rule.rationale: Described the Ba'ath as 'the leading party' and its theory as the leading theory of Iraqi society; no other political group was allowed to be active in the army, and the Communists were expelled from the National Front.

party-commands-army.rationale: Stated that the armed forces receive their orders from the Party and that no political group other than the Ba'ath Party is permitted to be active inside them, citing the Charter of National Action.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Purged Ba'ath officials at the 22 July 1979 meeting (22 executed), expelled the Communists from the Front, and banned independent political organisation; told the press that those who stand against national sovereignty will be dealt with.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Ordered the 1979 party purge, with summary treason trials and executions, and treated treason as a matter where Iraqi 'washes his hands' of the person.

party-controls-media.rationale: Iraqi media were controlled by the state and ruling party; independent assembly and parties were not permitted.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The constitution under his rule says the state alone establishes the armed forces and no other group may form military or paramilitary formations.

conscription.rationale: The constitution under his rule makes conscription compulsory and calls defence of the homeland a sacred duty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: As president he was commander-in-chief (told the FBI he devised the Kuwait invasion plan and the Khafji attack) and named his own ministers and cabinet.

separated-powers.rationale: Iraq's constitution made the Revolutionary Command Council, which he chaired, the supreme institution issuing laws with the force of law and electing the president, with immunity for its members.

strong-leader.rationale: Concentrated power in the presidency after 1979; told the FBI that until 1995 'the revolution brought me' and that he considered himself superior to those around him.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Held the presidency from 1979 until 2003 with no term limit and confirmed it by referendums in 1995 and 2002.

term-limits.rationale: Held office for 24 years with no limit and told the FBI that the people elected him in 1995 and 2002 and he owed them obligation; accepted no term limit.

leader-cult.rationale: A cult of personality built around him as father of the nation under his presidency, with portraits, statues and mass praise; he accepted and promoted it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Fought Ayatollah Khomeini's rule by clerics in Iran (the 1980 war), spoke of striking 'this turban', and opposed the Shia Islamist Dawa and SCIRI parties that sought clerical government.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Told the FBI that after the 1995 and 2002 votes 'the people did, in fact, vote for and elect' him and he owed them obligation, but the votes were single-candidate referendums and he took power through the RCC.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The constitution says the people are the source of authority and legitimacy, and he said the Iraqi people would not accept a leader chosen under occupation; his own rule rested on coercion and single-candidate referendums.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Described Iraqi democracy as 'people's democracy' expressed by consultation, newspaper discussion and an assembly of Ba'athist-led membership, not by competitive elections.

natural-rulers.rationale: Inferred: the FBI summary records that he considered himself an excellent debater and superior to those around him, and he ruled as the unrivalled leader; he did not state a doctrine of natural rulers.

right-to-secede.rationale: The constitution states Iraq's territory is indivisible and no part can be ceded; he used force against Kurdish and Shia rebellions.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Fought Barzani's Kurdish rebellion, crushed the 1991 Kurdish and Shia uprisings, and ran the 1988 Anfal campaign against Kurdish areas.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Led the 1970 Manifesto and 1974 Autonomous Region law for Kurdistan and called the autonomy a good arrangement in 1980, but later Arabised areas and attacked the Kurds.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The constitution prohibits any activity against the objectives of the people and he banned the Dawa Party and expelled the Communists from the Front for violating its principles.

more-religion-public.rationale: Launched the 1993 Faith Campaign: Qur'an a core school subject, alcohol curbed, Islamic punishments, takbir on the flag, new mosques. Scholars dispute whether this was belief or regime strategy.

separate-church-state.rationale: Told the FBI in 2004 that religion and government should not mix and that Ba'athism was not religious, but his regime made Islam central from 1991 and added Sharia punishments in 1994.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The 1993 Faith Campaign and 1994 decrees introduced Sharia-based penalties such as amputation, though the legal system stayed largely civil-law based.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: His government's Ministry of Endowments appointed clergy and approved mosque building and publications; he suppressed independent Shia clerical leadership.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Said he was a believer in God and his government rejected Marxist atheism, later promoting Islamic instruction instead.

religion-illusion.rationale: Told the FBI he was a believer in God though not a zealot, and in the 1990s his government promoted religion through the Faith Campaign; he did not present religion as an illusion that fades.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Said he believed in God and spoke of obligation to the people 'in front of God'; Ba'athist ideology joined science with faith in the Arab message.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Made Qur'an study a core subject in the national curriculum under the Faith Campaign and trained about 30,000 religion teachers.

traditional-family.rationale: Called the family 'a living cell' of society and the constitution calls it the nucleus of society to be protected by the state, while rejecting feudal views confining women to the home.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Urged stricter and wider conditions on divorce and said unjustified divorce should be condemned everywhere, as part of improving women's position.

women-suffrage.rationale: Declared women one half of society entitled to full participation; his government gave women full suffrage and the right to hold office, and women served as ministers and directors-general.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Said women's radical emancipation cannot be achieved without emancipating the whole society politically, economically and culturally, and that bourgeois concepts of emancipation will not free women.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Said obstacles in the way of women are greater than those facing men and condemned feudal, tribal and bourgeois outlooks that treat women as second class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Demanded equality of rights and rejected second-class status, yet said women are less suited to permanent combat service and better suited than men to childcare, and favoured balance rather than identical treatment.

equal-conscription.rationale: Said women's inability to serve on a large scale and permanently in combat units does not undermine equality and that men are better suited to the army; conscription applied to men.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Said the Agrarian Reform Law made no distinction between men and women; inheritance remained governed by the law as the constitution guarantees it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution under his rule declares citizens equal before the law regardless of sex, origin, language or religion, while his regime persecuted Kurds, Shia and opponents.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The constitution under his rule makes social solidarity the first foundation, with each citizen accomplishing duty in full and the state guaranteeing rights; defence of the homeland is a sacred duty.

person-over-state.rationale: Described the human being, man or woman, as the basic instrument of the party's struggle and called on citizens to sacrifice for the revolution.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Repeatedly invoked Iraq's six-thousand-year civilization and Arab heritage and wrote national pride in heritage into education aims.

patriotic-education.rationale: The constitution lists as education's aim a generation 'proud of his people, his homeland and heritage' and he promoted it.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Presented Iraq as 'a civilization of six thousand years' and his state tied Babylonian and Assyrian heritage to Arab nationalism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Described the Arab nation as 'in a state of renaissance' and beginning to rise after being kept backward.

class-struggle-history.rationale: His government opposed orthodox Marxist class conflict and held that class divisions in the Arab world run along national lines.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Ba'athism under him rejected the dictatorship of the proletariat and Marxist atheism, while he expelled the Communists from the National Front.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Said each nation has its own particular programme and form of socialism and that Iraq's democracy and laws must suit its developing conditions.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Told the FBI the 1948 formation of a separate Jewish state created the problem and that a Palestinian state is the basis of any solution; the war with Israel was 'still on'. His speeches call Israel the 'Zionist entity'.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Called Israel a 'Zionist entity' and the 1948 formation of Israel the 'rape of Palestine' and an aggression against the Arab nation, but did not use the term colonial project.

civilizational-union.rationale: Constitution and speeches state the basic objective of realising one Arab state; told the FBI the Arab nation is one nation with the same language, borders and aims.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Called for Arab unity as the goal of the Ba'ath revolution and said there is one Arab world from the simple person to the thinker.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Said the Arab nation, from poor to wealthy, is one nation with the same language, common borders and aims, despite state borders.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pursued Arab unity and claimed Kuwait as Iraq's rightful 19th province, saying British interference split it from Iraq.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Justified the Kuwait claim by saying Kuwait had been separated from Iraq by British interference, rejecting the colonial-era arrangement.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Rejected the Iraq-Kuwait border drawn under British influence and annexed Kuwait in 1990.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Invaded Iran in 1980 and Kuwait in 1990, declaring Kuwait Iraq's 19th province.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Cited Iraq's goal of regaining the Shatt al-Arab and abrogated the 1975 Algiers Agreement in 1980; also claimed Kuwait as historically Iraqi.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Planned and ordered the 1980 invasion of Iran and told the FBI he devised the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

force-without-un.rationale: Ordered the 1980 invasion of Iran and the 1990 invasion of Kuwait without any UN authorisation, and told the FBI Iraq could respond to US strikes without waiting for the UN.

military-superiority.rationale: Built one of the region's largest armies; told the FBI Iraq could not appear weak to regional enemies and said its army should serve the entire Arab nation.

empower-police-military.rationale: Expanded the army, security forces and secret police; told the FBI he treated Iraq's defence as central.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Urged Arab states not to give military bases to any foreign power and called Omani base offers to the Americans unacceptable.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Said Iraq relies on nobody except Iraq and the Arab nation, belonged to the Non-Aligned Movement and rejected following either superpower.

dominated-front.rationale: Urged solidarity among Third World and non-aligned countries to protect independence from superpowers, while keeping friendship with the USSR.

collective-defense.rationale: Backed the National Declaration under which Arab states fight together against any foreigner who attacks Arab land or interests.

national-self-determination.rationale: Said 'we believe in the right of people to self-determination' (about Iran), yet he denied Kurds a state and annexed Kuwait.

multipolar-world.rationale: Told the FBI a world of two superpowers was better than now but argued that strengthening Third World and non-aligned countries would blunt superpower spheres of influence.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Told the FBI the UN had exceeded its authority and charter regarding Iraq and that sanctions followed US positions; he rejected UN inspections for years.

nation-first.rationale: Stressed Iraq's sovereignty and dignity over outside demands and ignored the Security Council on Kuwait, while saying he wanted a relationship with the US.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Told the FBI that Iran intended to annex southern Iraq and that the US and 'Zionist' influence conspired against Iraq.

population-transfer.rationale: Said in 1980 'We have expelled some people of Iranian affiliation'; his government deported Feyli Kurds and Arabised Kirkuk.

majority-settlement.rationale: His government's Arabisation policy moved Arabs into Kirkuk and other Kurdish areas and displaced Kurds in Anfal.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Asked whether Iraq aided Arabs, Kurds and Bakhtiar followers in Iran he said opposition members who came to Iraq received a 'double greeting'; Iraq backed Iranian opposition during the war.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Defended Iraq's nuclear technology programme with France and Italy as aimed at peaceful uses and said the atom is widely used for peaceful purposes.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Rejected the Iraqi Special Tribunal's legitimacy and criticised UN authority over Iraq, but never stated that domestic law outranks international law generally.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Called Israeli control of Arab lands occupation and demanded UN resolutions be enforced, while annexing Kuwait himself, so his stance is contested.

revolution-justified.rationale: Took part in the 1959 assassination attempt, the 1963 and 1968 Ba'ath coups, and called the 1968 revolution the foundation of the state.

political-violence-never.rationale: Personally led political violence and executions including the 1968 removals and the 1979 purge.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: His Ba'ath group, a small armed party, seized power by coup in 1968, but he did not state a general theory of vanguard armed groups.

death-penalty.rationale: Presided over a state that executed convicts and opponents, including 22 Ba'athists in 1979 after a treason trial and capital penalties for desertion and corruption in 1994.

notes: Views changed: the 1970s-80s sources are secular Ba'athist; from 1991 and the 1993 Faith Campaign the regime promoted Islam, but in 2004 he told the FBI religion and government should not mix. Where acts contradict stated principles (equal citizenship, self-determination, democracy), answers are low or 0. Not reached: The Saddam Tapes (Woods, Palkki, Stout), Conflict Records Research Center files, and Social and Foreign Affairs in Iraq (restricted on the Internet Archive); the Al-Khuld Hall tape and Anfal are used only through Wikipedia.
